USA.hook: The only country with land borders on just two nations yet coastline on three oceans — the Arctic one courtesy of Alaska, bought from Russia for two cents an acre.
USA.place: The wide middle of North America, Canada above and Mexico below, with Alaska detached in the far northwest corner.

CAN.hook: Has the longest coastline of any country on Earth — about 202,000km, roughly a sixth of the world's total, thanks to a shattered Arctic archipelago.
CAN.place: Everything above the United States, ocean to ocean to ocean. The border it shares with the US is the longest between any two countries.

MEX.hook: Mexico City is sinking as much as 50cm a year in places — it was built on a drained lake bed, and the ground is still compacting under it.
MEX.place: The funnel narrowing southeast from the US border down to the Central American chain.

GTM.hook: The world's largest exporter of cardamom, a spice barely used in its own kitchens — almost the entire crop is shipped to the Middle East.
GTM.place: The first link in the Central American chain, directly south of Mexico.

BLZ.hook: The only Central American country with English as its official language, and home to the largest barrier reef in the northern hemisphere.
BLZ.place: The small notch on the Caribbean side, east of Guatemala and just below Mexico's Yucatán.

HND.hook: The original banana republic — the phrase was coined for it in 1904, when US fruit companies effectively ran the country.
HND.place: The wide part of the isthmus, between Guatemala and Nicaragua, with a long Caribbean coast.

SLV.hook: The smallest country in mainland Americas, and the only one in Central America with no Caribbean coast at all.
SLV.place: Pacific side only, wedged between Guatemala and Honduras.

NIC.hook: Largest country in Central America, and its lake has bull sharks — they swim up the San Juan river from the Caribbean and stay.
NIC.place: The middle of the isthmus, between Honduras and Costa Rica.

CRI.hook: Abolished its army in 1948 and put the money into schools and hospitals — it has not had one since.
CRI.place: Between Nicaragua and Panama, near the bottom of the isthmus.

PAN.hook: The isthmus runs east-west, not north-south — so in Panama City the sun rises over the Pacific and sets over the Atlantic.
PAN.place: The S-bend at the bottom of Central America, joining the continent to Colombia.
